body.statement: Along every sequence in \(\mathcal M_N\) with \(\inf_N\mu_D>0\), the canonical gradient for \(\theta_T\) is the minimum-variance allocated influence score for \(Y-\theta_TD\), divided by \(\mu_D\), and its source-sample variance is \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)/\mu_D^2\). The profiled Anderson--Rubin interval is first-order equivalent to the efficient Wald interval generated by \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\).
body.justification: The identification-robust procedure remains efficient under strong compliance.
body.gap: Rudolph and van der Laan derive a single-source ratio gradient, while Su et al. derive multi-source weights for a nonratio effect; neither gives the joint residual allocation.
body.consumer: Regular multi-site analyses sacrifice no first-order precision by using robust inversion.
